name: Sun
summary: Our star, a middle-aged yellow dwarf ~4.6 billion years old that holds 99.86% of the solar system's mass.
sound_desc: The Sun rings like a bell: SOHO measured acoustic waves bouncing inside it (helioseismology), which, sped up, become an audible low hum.

name: Proxima Centauri
summary: The nearest star to the Sun, a flaring red dwarf with at least one Earth-mass planet in its habitable zone.
sound_desc: Space is a near-perfect vacuum, so no sound travels through it. Stars do 'ring' with internal sound waves (asteroseismology, measured by Kepler and TESS), but no sonification of this star is widely available.
